paper.title: A Judge Should Know What Changed:Construct Validity for LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation
paper.abstract: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation is usually assessed by agreement and robustness to surface perturbations, but reliability does not establish construct validity. We formalize construct validity for an evaluator as a two-dimensional profile: invariance S, the probability that a verdict is unchanged under construct-preserving edits, and construct sensitivity R, the probability that it changes under minimal construct-changing edits. We show that S and R are independent and that no scalar summary preserves

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的不是“评审模型稳不稳”，而是更基础的“评审模型到底有没有在测它声称要测的东西”。作者指出，现有 LLM-as-a-Judge 研究大多只测不变性：当答案长度、格式、候选顺序、作者元信息等表面属性变化，而真实质量不变时，judge 是否保持判决不变。但一个评测器即便在这些扰动下很稳定，也可能根本感知不到真正的质量变化。为此，论文把 construct validity 明确拆成两个独立维度：S 表示对不改变构念的编辑保持不变，R 表示对最小但真正改变构念的编辑产生响应。作者选取“科学表述是否超出证据支持范围”作为可操作构念，并进一步把 overreach 分成 scope 和 strength 两类最小编辑，检验 judge 是否真的能分辨这两种变化。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接启发不在训练方法，而在评测信号质量。现在很多 post-train、reward model、judge-based preference data、self-improvement pipeline 都默认 judge 分数可当作训练目标或筛选信号。这篇工作提醒：高一致性、高相关性、低表面偏置，并不等于评测器在测目标构念。如果 R 低，拿这样的 judge 去做偏好蒸馏、RL 奖励、数据过滤，模型会学到“与标签生成条件相关的表面代理变量”，而不是目标能力本身。这个判断对 reward hacking、合成偏好数据、自动化评测闭环都很关键。贡献量级属于评测方法论层面的纠偏：不是提出一个更强 judge，而是给出一套更严格的 judge 有效性定义、可测协议，以及对现有公开评测集‘可验证头寸’的分析框架。
summary.technical_approach: 方法上有三层。第一层是形式化。作者把 evaluator 的 construct validity 定义为二维 profile (S, R)，并证明两点：其一，S 和 R 相互独立，不能用一个标量替代；其二，如果不知道 S，仅看 R 没有解释意义，因为一个对任何输入都乱变的 judge 也可能表现出表面上的“敏感”。因此他们引入 validity frontier，而不是单分数排序。第二层是干预设计。作者围绕 scientific overclaim 构造两类最小编辑：scope edit 改变命题适用范围，如从特定条件推广到更广人群、从一次观察改写成稳定性质、加强量词；strength edit 不改变适用范围，但提高断言强度，如去掉条件、去掉 hedge、加入 evidence 不支持的 intensifier。每个编辑方向由人工标注确定，避免把“哪边更过度”交给模型自己判断。第三层是测量与验证。作者在 7 个 judges、4 个领域上测量 S 与 R，并单独分析 scope/strength 两轴；同时提出 validation power，强调评测集是否给 judge 留出了“只能依赖构念、不能靠生成来源或表面模式猜标签”的空间。这里的关键点是 paired mode：把同一基础样本的最小编辑对拿出来看，才能真正测到 sensitivity；若只按 item 独立评估，很多数据集会因为 provenance leakage 看起来很可靠，实际并不能检验 construct sensitivity。文中还重跑了 Peters and Chin-Yee 关于 accuracy prompting 会加剧 overgeneralization 的现象，发现其效果在 scope 与 strength 两轴上方向相反，从而解释了原先看似矛盾的结果。
summary.experiments: 关键实验结论有三类。第一，7 个 judge 在 4 个领域上的 profile 显示：不少模型在 invariance 上并不差，但在 construct sensitivity 上明显不足，而且这种不足不是均匀的。对 overclaim 的两种编辑，judge 往往对 strength 更敏感、对 scope 更迟钝，说明它们更容易抓住“语气更强了”这种表层 certainty 信号，而不容易抓住“适用范围被偷偷放大了”这种语义外延变化。第二，accuracy pressure 的复现实验表明，要求模型“更准确”会让 judge 对 strength 方向更宽容或更偏向高确定性表述，同时对 scope 的反应不同，这解释了为什么先前工作会观察到“追求准确反而更过度泛化”。第三，作者在 5 个公开数据集上测 validation power，并比较 item mode 与 paired mode。结论是模式差异很大：同一批数据按单样本看似合理，但转成成对最小编辑后，只有约 55%–67% 的标签信息可恢复，说明大量公开 judge 校准集其实允许模型靠来源、长度、生成条件等旁路特征解题，而不是靠目标构念。摘要里提到的 541,000 次 judgment 上 verbosity bias 很小，与另一资源中“只看长度比 judge 更能复现标签”并不矛盾；作者给出的解释是后者标签本身泄漏了生成条件，问题在数据，不全在 judge。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读时先看 §2 和定义部分，抓住 S、R、validity frontier、validation power 这几个概念，否则后面的实验容易被当成又一篇 judge bias 论文。然后看 §3.1 对 scope / strength 的区分，这里是全文最有信息量的地方，因为它把“过度概括”拆成了两个机制不同的轴。实验部分建议重点看 §4 的 profile 图和按轴拆分结果，再看 §4.4 与 §5.4 关于 public sets 的 paired-vs-item 分析，这部分对做自动评测、reward model 数据构造的人最有用。预计 30–45 分钟能抓住主线；若关心 RLHF / RLAIF / judge-based filtering，值得把定义、命题和数据集分析细读一遍。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper asks a more basic question than judge reliability: does an LLM judge actually respond to the construct it claims to measure? Prior work mostly tests invariance—whether verdicts stay unchanged when length, formatting, candidate order, or metadata change while quality does not. That only covers one half of validity. A judge can be stable and still be blind to the target construct. The authors formalize construct validity as a two-dimensional profile: S for invariance under construct-preserving edits, and R for responsiveness to minimal construct-changing edits. They instantiate this on scientific overclaiming, where minimal edits are well defined, and further separate overclaim into scope changes and strength changes.
summary_en.importance: The main value for foundation-model research is about evaluation signal quality. Many post-training pipelines, reward models, synthetic preference datasets, and self-improvement loops implicitly treat judge scores as usable supervision. This paper shows that low surface bias and decent agreement are not enough. If construct sensitivity is weak, the judge can still reward proxies tied to data provenance or style rather than the intended capability. That matters directly for reward hacking, automated data filtering, and judge-based RL or distillation. The contribution is methodological rather than model-building: a stricter validity framework, an intervention-based measurement protocol, and a way to quantify whether public evaluation sets even have enough headroom to reveal sensitivity failures.
summary_en.technical_approach: The method has three pieces. First, a formalization: evaluator validity is represented as a pair (S, R), not a single scalar. The paper argues and proves that the two coordinates are independent, and that R is not interpretable without S, because a noisy judge can appear responsive for the wrong reasons. This motivates a validity frontier instead of one-number ranking. Second, an intervention design around scientific overclaiming. The authors define scope edits that widen the set of situations a claim covers—broader populations, adjacent domains, stronger quantifiers, turning an observation into a standing property. They define strength edits that keep scope fixed but increase commitment—removing conditions, deleting hedges, adding unsupported intensifiers. Edit direction is set by human annotators rather than inferred from model outputs. Third, a measurement and validation protocol. They evaluate 7 judges across 4 domains, separately scoring invariance and sensitivity, and separately analyzing scope versus strength. They also introduce validation power, which asks whether a dataset forces the evaluator to rely on the construct rather than on provenance or surface cues. A key point is the distinction between item mode and paired mode: only paired minimal-edit evaluation can expose sensitivity failures that are invisible in ordinary per-item scoring. The paper also revisits the earlier finding that prompting for accuracy worsens overgeneralization, and shows that the effect differs by axis, resolving the apparent paradox.
summary_en.experiments: Three empirical findings stand out. First, the measured profiles show that several judges are not terrible on invariance but are weak on construct sensitivity, and the weakness is asymmetric. Judges tend to react more to strength edits than to scope edits, suggesting that they are better at detecting stronger-sounding certainty than at noticing semantic expansion of applicability. Second, the replication of accuracy pressure reveals opposite movement on the two axes, which explains why earlier work could observe more overgeneralization under an 'accuracy' prompt. Third, the validation-power analysis on 5 public datasets shows a large gap between item mode and paired mode. The same datasets can look acceptable when scored item by item, yet only about 55%–67% of the relevant signal is recoverable in paired form, indicating substantial leakage from generation conditions or other shortcuts. This also reconciles two seemingly conflicting observations mentioned in the introduction: negligible verbosity bias in a large audit versus a calibration set where length alone predicts labels better than the judge. The issue can lie in the label construction, not only in the judge.
summary_en.reading_guide: Start with the formal definitions in Section 2. The paper is easy to misread as another judge-bias audit unless the S/R split is clear. Then read the scope-versus-strength discussion in Section 3.1 carefully; that is where the construct becomes operational and where much of the paper’s insight sits. In the experiments, focus on the profile plots in Section 4 and the axis-specific breakdowns, then read the paired-versus-item analysis in Sections 4.4 and 5.4. That part is especially useful if you work on reward models, automated evaluation, or synthetic supervision. A skim read takes around 30–45 minutes; a closer read is worthwhile if your training loop depends on judge-generated labels.

recommendation.zh: 读 metric 定义和干预设计即可；它提醒自动 judge 的高稳定性可能只是迟钝，不应直接当 reward 信号质量。
recommendation.en: Read the metric definitions and intervention design; it usefully warns that a stable judge may simply be insensitive, not a good reward signal.

paper.title: RecurSE: Bounded Recursive Self-Evaluation for LLM Rubric Judges
paper.abstract: LLM-as-judge is essential for evaluating open-ended text and steering post-training, yet improving the judge itself typically relies on expensive annotations, reward models, or distillation from stronger teachers. In this work, we eliminate external gold supervision from the RL training reward: the model's own evaluative capability generates learning signals for its optimization -- a closed-loop setting of bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) termed Recursive Self-Evaluation (RecurSE). We st

summary.core_problem: 论文研究 LLM rubric judge 能否在没有外部 gold annotation、reward model 或强教师蒸馏的情况下，通过自身评估能力生成训练信号并改进。
summary.importance: 贡献是后训练与评测信号生成方法。它把 LLM-as-judge 的训练做成一个受限递归自评估闭环，直接触及 post-train 中奖励信号质量、self-improvement 边界和 reward hacking 风险。
summary.technical_approach: RecurSE 使用两阶段结构：Pass 1 中可训练 judge 按逐条 rubric 评价候选回答；Pass 2 中同步的 policy-copy checker 根据 meta-rubric 审计 judge 的推理，并输出标量 process reward。关键设计是 interface decoupling，将 checker 的标量分数与 judge 的 verdict tokens 结构隔离，避免模型通过复制或操纵判决 token 走捷径。
summary.experiments: 摘要说明论文研究“何时能自我改进、何时必须停止”，但未给出具体模型规模、训练数据、benchmark 名称和提升幅度。需要读正文确认 RL 设置、停止条件、是否有外部验证集以及 judge 泛化是否真实提升。
summary.authors_note: 作者来自浙江大学计算机科学与技术学院和美团 LongCat Team；Jieping Ye 是机器学习与数据挖掘方向的知名研究者。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies whether an LLM rubric judge can improve without external gold labels, reward models, or distillation from a stronger teacher.
summary_en.importance: Its contribution is a post-training method for generating judge-training rewards in a bounded self-evaluation loop. It is directly relevant to reward-signal quality, self-improvement limits, and reward hacking in LLM training.
summary_en.technical_approach: RecurSE uses two passes. In Pass 1, a trainable judge evaluates candidate responses under per-rule rubrics. In Pass 2, a synchronized policy-copy checker audits the judge’s reasoning against meta-rubrics and produces a scalar process reward. The key engineering choice is interface decoupling, which separates the checker’s scalar score from the judge’s verdict tokens to remove a token-copying shortcut.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract states that the paper studies when recursive self-improvement can occur and when it must stop, but does not provide model sizes, datasets, benchmark names, or improvement numbers. The full paper is needed to assess the RL setup, stopping criterion, validation protocol, and generalization of the judge.
summary_en.authors_note: The authors are affiliated with Zhejiang University and Meituan LongCat Team. Jieping Ye is a well-known researcher in machine learning and data mining.

recommendation.zh: 读方法和 failure analysis；若 stopping rule 干净，值得复现到内部 judge/RLVR 管线，否则只是自举奖励的又一个脆弱版本。
recommendation.en: Read the method and failure analysis; if the stopping rule is clean, it is worth reproducing in judge/RLVR pipelines, otherwise it is another fragile self-reward loop.
